children.text: Egocentric Assistant for Clinical Perception and Action

MedXRAgent is an XR-supported, context-aware clinical agent for outpatient encounters. It integrates streamed dialogue, egocentric visual observations, structured patient context, EHR-derived history when available, and web-grounded medical evidence through a perception-understanding-context-reasoning loop.

To evaluate evidence-grounded egocentric clinical assistance, the project curates MedXR-Bench from NEJM Image Challenge cases, with 795 training and 271 test egocentric video cases. MedXRAgent achieves the best open-ended diagnosis score on the test split, and ablations show that both visual and web evidence substantially improve diagnosis performance, supporting it as a research framework rather than an autonomous diagnostic system.

GazeAgent supports query-driven analysis of gaze behavior in naturalistic interactions, helping practitioners answer semantic and temporal questions about attention targets, gaze durations, and gaze shifts without relying on intrusive sensing setups or labor-intensive post-hoc workflows.

The system transforms raw interaction data into a semantically grounded, temporally aligned gaze timeline, then uses a code-generating agent to translate natural-language queries into executable analyses. This design enables precise, interpretable computation of gaze statistics and temporal relationships, reducing analysis workload while improving task efficiency and confidence in interpreting gaze behavior.
GazeAgent: Querying Children’s Gaze Behavior in Psychological Assessment Interaction

GazeAgent is an AR-based interactive system that helps clinicians and researchers analyze children’s gaze behavior during naturalistic assessment interactions. Using observer-worn smart glasses, the system captures interaction videos, grounds gaze into semantic targets such as toys, faces, and eye contact, and answers natural-language queries with concise timelines and visual evidence.
Accepted as a CVPR 2026 Demonstration, the system presents query-driven gaze analysis as an interactive workflow for psychological assessment contexts.
Egocentric Assistant for Clinical Perception and Action

EgoMedAgent explores how augmented reality can make medical AI more interactive, contextual, and human-centered. Developed in the context of the MedGemma Impact Challenge, the project builds on MedGemma, Google’s open model for multimodal medical text and image comprehension, and reimagines it as an embodied assistant that can operate in a first-person AR setting. By combining AR interaction with healthcare-focused multimodal reasoning, EgoMedAgent points toward a more intuitive form of medical AI, one that can ground assistance in what the user is seeing and make complex medical information more accessible in real-world workflows.

attrs.alt: Overview of the developmental learning paradigm for multimodal LLMs

children.text: Position: Multimodal LLMs Should Learn from Children

This position paper explores how multimodal AI can move beyond static dataset fitting toward a more developmental, child-inspired learning paradigm. Rather than treating intelligence as performance on fixed benchmarks, the paper argues that next-generation MLLMs should learn more like children: by forming their own learning tasks, inferring supervision from weak multimodal signals, and growing continuously without catastrophic forgetting.

By connecting cognitive science with modern multimodal learning through egocentric first-person data, social scaffolding, language-based feedback, and memory-augmented adaptation, the work outlines a roadmap toward AI systems that are more adaptive, data-efficient, physically grounded, and robust in open-world settings.
AudioGuard: Toward Comprehensive Audio Safety Protection Across Diverse Threat Models

AudioGuard introduces a more realistic way to safeguard voice AI by going beyond transcript-only moderation. It combines waveform-level audio understanding with ASR-based content moderation to detect risks that text alone can miss, such as harmful non-speech sound events, child voice and impersonation cues, and voice-content compositional harms. The system is built alongside AUDIOSAFETYBENCH, a policy-grounded benchmark with 10K+ labeled audio samples, 17 languages, and 50+ speaker identities, covering both audio-input and audio-output safety in real-world settings like voice assistants, voice cloning, and interactive audio agents. Across this benchmark and four complementary audio safety benchmarks, AudioGuard delivers stronger accuracy and lower latency than monolithic audio-LLM guardrails, making it a practical and interpretable solution for real-world voice safety.
